newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle markets quiet Monday - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle markets quiet Monday - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet early Monday, with several beef packing plants closed for the Veterans Day holiday, according to feedlot sources.
IBP said its plants at Amarillo, Texas; Emporia, Kan.; and West Point, Neb., would be closed. National Beef Packing also said its Liberal, Kan., plant would be closed.

Showlists this week reportedly were about unchnaged from a week ago and still containing a large percentage of cattle that have only been on feed 100 days or less, according to several feedlot managers.

Packer buying interest was extremely light following last week's active session which saw most showlists bought at $72.00 per cwt. Cattle owners this week were asking $73.00 to $74.00. Packer bids were expected to surface at $72.00.

Prices this week were expected to be bolstered by active beef movement Friday and outlooks for continued strong beef demand this week. There were 303 fabricated loads sold Friday, according to USDA. Prices continued to reflect tight supplies of choice cattle. Choice cuts were quoted up $0.86 to $0.96 and selects were down $0.49 to $0.95, according to USDA.
